belief: Caring for others means my needs don't count.
origins: Parents, caregivers for aging relatives, and people in helping professions often learn to put themselves last. Family messages like “Don’t be selfish” or religious teaching that confuses sacrifice with self-erasure can add to it. Over time, we may stop noticing our own needs, grow tired and resentful, and still feel guilty for wanting anything.
teaches: Jesus said the second great commandment is to love our neighbor as ourselves, which assumes that we also care for ourselves. Paul says no one ever hated his own body, but nourishes and cherishes it. Paul also says to look not only to our own interests, but also to the interests of others, which means both. When Elijah was exhausted, God let him sleep and sent an angel to say, “Get up and eat.” Caring for ourselves is not selfish. It is how we keep loving others.
self_statements: Taking time for myself is selfish.
If I stop, everything will fall apart.
Good people do not have needs.
errors: Insisting that I must always put others first.
Believing that I must either serve others or be selfish.
Feeling guilty and concluding that I am wrong to rest.
Treating a short break as a failure of love.
questions: Where did I learn that my needs do not count?
What would happen to the people I love if I became exhausted or ill?
What does “love your neighbor as yourself” say about how I treat myself?
What do I need most right now?
Who could share some of the load?
What is one small way I can care for myself this week?
truth: My needs count to God, and caring for myself helps me keep loving others. I can care for the people in my life without erasing myself and can ask for help without guilt.
hw_truths: Love your neighbor as yourself includes me.
I can care for others and for myself.
log: Each day, name one need you had and one small way you met it or asked for help.
actions: Write physical, emotional, and spiritual needs you have been ignoring.
Choose one task to hand off to someone else this week.
Put a block of rest or enjoyment on the calendar.
Ask God to show you how to love yourself as He does.
prayer: Lord, You care for the one who cares for others. Forgive me for ignoring my needs. Show me how to love my neighbor and myself, and give me the grace to ask for help. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did I learn that my needs do not count?
What do I need right now?
What happens if I run out of strength?
What is one small act of self-care?
How can I ask for help this week?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can love my neighbor as myself, so my needs matter too.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Caring for others means my needs don't count.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
